summary_paragraph: A female patient with a history of paraplegia from a gunshot wound, neurogenic bladder, and homelessness presented with worsening numbness and pain in her lower extremities after spending multiple nights on the street. She was diagnosed with mild (first-degree) frostbite of the right foot, likely due to cold exposure, and was managed with pain control, wound care, and tetanus prophylaxis. Vascular surgery recommended no surgical intervention. A urine culture showed only yeast, consistent with colonization rather than bacterial infection, so she was treated with a short course of fluconazole and discontinued from antibiotics to avoid resistance. She also had a stage II pressure ulcer on her heel and chronic pain related to her spinal injury. Despite recommendations for discharge to a shelter with nursing support or visiting nurse services, she insisted on going to a friend’s house and was discharged with wound care instructions, pain medications, and close follow-up advice. Her condition was stable at discharge.
problems: Accident due to excessive cold due to weather conditions
Late effect of spinal cord injury
Late effects of injury purposely inflicted by other person
